articles.title_en: Lionel Messi Plans a Grand Farewell as His Argentina Era Draws to a Close.
articles.title_ru: Лионель Месси готовит грандиозное прощание, завершая эпоху в сборной Аргентины.
articles.preview_en: Lionel Messi will end his Argentina career with a friendly against Benin.
articles.preview_ru: Лионель Месси завершит карьеру в сборной Аргентины товарищеским матчем против Бенина.
articles.full_en: Lionel Messi will conclude his Argentina career in a friendly match against Benin next month. The 39‑year‑old forward announced the farewell fixture during a press conference in Buenos Aires. Argentina’s football federation scheduled the game as a symbolic send‑off after the World Cup triumph. Messi’s decision marks the end of a golden era that produced three Copa América titles and a World Cup victory. Analysts predict his retirement will open opportunities for younger talents to shape the national team’s future. Fans worldwide plan celebrations and tributes, while sponsors prepare new marketing strategies without the iconic figure. Messi’s final appearance will be remembered as a historic moment that inspires generations of footballers.
articles.full_ru: Лионель Месси завершит карьеру в сборной Аргентины в товарищеском матче против Бенина в следующем месяце. Тридцатидевятилетний нападающий объявил о прощальном матче во время прессконференции в Буэнос-Айресе. Футбольный союз Аргентины назначил игру как символическое прощание после триумфа на чемпионате мира. Решение Месси ознаменовало конец золотой эры, принесшей три титула КопаАмерика и чемпионат мира. Эксперты прогнозируют, что его уход откроет путь молодым талантам сформировать будущее национальной команды. Болельщики по всему миру планируют празднования и трибьюты, а спонсоры разрабатывают новые маркетинговые стратегии без звёздного игрока. Последнее появление Месси запомнится как исторический момент, вдохновляющий поколения футболистов.

articles.title_en: The 90s: Art and Fashion review – this isn’t an exhibition, it’s a magazine spread
articles.title_ru: The 90s: Art and Fashion review – this isn’t an exhibition, it’s a magazine spread
articles.preview_en: Tate Britain, London The Young British Art of the 1990s was brash and macabre but also intelligent and emotional.
articles.preview_ru: Tate Britain, London The Young British Art of the 1990s was brash and macabre but also intelligent and emotional.
articles.full_en: Tate Britain, London The Young British Art of the 1990s was brash and macabre but also intelligent and emotional. This breathlessly superficial show reduces it to a stylish pose Jake and Dinos Chapman were dismissed by some even in the 1990s as overgrown adolescents selling shock for its own sake, and yet it is their work that brings this dismally shallow show closest to a moment of depth. Their sculpture Great Deeds Against the Dead, based on a print of Napoleonic war atrocities by Goya, is a display of dismembered, bleeding nude corpses hung on a tree. It asks questions about war and art, the representation of pain, whether art can have a moral purpose. The best British art of the 1990s was like that, coming on as brash, vulgar, macabre, yet also unexpectedly intelligent and emotional. Unfortunately this show is neither. You’d think Tate Britain would want to do justice to a decade in which these Millbank premises played a starring role, staging the Turner prize in the years when bisected cows, concrete houses and elephant dung got the nation arguing.
